name: Static Cling
beta: Begin as for the neighboring Giz Gaz and take the left one of a pair of matching flake cracks through the bulge; on the second pitch you ascend the block above while clipping a pin and a few bolts.
overview: Takes the left one of two alike flake-cracks through the bulge. On pitch two you tackle the block overhead.

current.location: begins the same as Gaz Giz

name: Trapeze Left
beta: Bolts lead up to a lengthy roof; work leftward past more bolts to get around its left end, then keep going up the wall above it.
overview: Bolts lead to an extended overhang, which you cross leftward past more bolts before pulling over at its left end. Face climbing above then continues, keeping well west of the crack known as Upper Right Ski Track.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Inverted Staircase
beta: About 500 feet of climbing gains a broad ledge; shift right, then go up and slightly right, clipping three bolts on the way to the ceilings. Easier ground then eases toward the slabs below the top.
overview: An intimidating line up steep, broken rock immediately to the right of the large arch low on the north face. The crux is the Staircase itself, a stack of three ceilings arranged like steps, where it gets desperately hard; above, the going eases.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Is that a Munchkin in your Pocket
beta: Stay on the arete standing to the left of a clean corner that faces right; higher up, step off it to the left. A single bolt sits at the start.
overview: Toprope the arete to the left of the tidy corner, drifting left higher up; one bolt sits at the start.

current.area_walk_in: The southwest-facing wall sits over the hill from the Oz Towers; go up and left from the Poppie Field Boulders.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: 50 ft up and right of Baby Rattler, beside a tidy corner

name: Junglework
beta: Stay on the Egghead line until just beyond its second bolt, then drift five feet right and go directly up.
overview: A top-rope line (follows Egghead past its second bolt, then veers right about five feet and goes straight up).

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: follows Egghead past its second bolt, then veers right about five feet and goes straight up

name: Keebler's Revenge
beta: The route is a sustained, technical pumper from the first clip to the anchor, and some climbers rate it harder than its number suggests.
overview: Six bolts of sustained, technical climbing that feels harder than its grade.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Kingsnake
beta: Cross leftward along ledges from the crag's right end, tackle the overhang by its two bolts, then angle up and leftward past one more bolt to meet Sidewinder for that route's closing traverse.
overview: Shuffle leftward over ledges starting at the crag's right-hand side, surmount the overhang with two bolts, then veer upward leftward by one further bolt, meeting Sidewinder for its closing traverse.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: over an overhang; joins Sidewinder's final traverse

name: Kodiak
beta: Keep an eye out for bolt number four: it blends in with the rock and is set well to the right.
overview: A bolted face of hard pinches and crimps that finishes on a ledge at the foot of the Bear Arete.

current.area_walk_in: Head up the fire road past the cliff, then take the narrow trail that doubles back through manzanita; allow 20 to 45 minutes from the road.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.anchor: two-bolt station on the terrace below Bear Arete

name: Krokus
beta: Protect the crack under the second bolt with gear in the 2 to 3 inch range, in addition to the bolts.
overview: Short bolted route on soft sandstone that has been climbed so often it has changed noticeably over the past decade.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Lascivious Conduct
beta: Work up the deep scoops close to the crag's left margin, clipping three bolts.
overview: A bolted line up steeply scooped rock near the crag's left margin.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: near the left margin of the crag

name: Lava Falls
beta: Supplement the bolts with large nuts, sizes 4 to 5, and slings tied off around knobs.
overview: A long, steep route that is surprisingly moderate for its angle, demanding sustained focus as you work up water-scrubbed grooves on knobs.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Lazy Bum
beta:
Most parties stop after the first pitch, where the crack thins and you are pushed left to reach a far-off edge.

Gear to about 2 inches works, especially very small pieces under 1 inch.
overview: A two-star 5.10d on Sunnyside Bench; many parties stop after the first pitch.

current.area_walk_in: Walk the Lower Yosemite Fall trail to the bridge, cross it, and continue a short way east. A climbers' path leaves the trail and a brief scramble gets you to the foot of the cliff.

name: Leader's Fright
beta: Placing protection is tricky for a typical leader at this standard.

name: Lee's Health Studio (aka The Dehab Clinic)
beta: Follow the brown dike as it slants leftward, passing three bolts that have chain-link hangers, and then continue by a fixed pin.
overview: Tracks a brown dike leaning leftward, clipping three bolts, then reaches a fixed pin.

current.location: some 100 yards beyond Blood And Cuts, heading rightward

name: Lieback and Lingerie
beta: Layback a slim flake leaning to the right, clipping two bolts, then continue upward until reaching the final bolt of Sexy Sady.
overview: A thin flake leaning to the right clips two bolts, then rises to merge with Sexy Sadye at her last bolt.

name: Light Touch
beta: Clip two bolts and then ascend the thin crack above.
overview: The leftmost line on its wall: a pair of bolts followed by a thin crack.

name: Lithium
beta: The anchor is partly concealed, roughly 40 ft over the final bolt and a touch right, beneath the overhang. Shorter climbers will find the moves harder.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Little Caesar
beta: Three bolts protect it, the last one set high toward the face's upper right corner, off to the right of the following route's upper part.
overview: Its third bolt is placed very high toward the upper right, far above the preceding moves.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Los Tres Bovines
beta: Begin by traversing rightward from the neighboring route's start, then climb past three bolts and step left at the last one. The first bolt is a long way up.
overview: Begins at the previous route, traverses right, then ascends three bolts, shifting left at the last. Runout before the first bolt.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Lost Boys
beta: Clip three bolts, then step left into Czech Cows Say Boo's upper crack.
overview: A short line inside the corridor, launched off a boulder, that links into its neighbor's top crack.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Rumbling Rampart
beta: Follow the prominent water chute up the back of the formation. The rock gets a little better to the left once past the third bolt, where the crux is.
overview: Runs up the conspicuous waterchute on the formation's rear side, inside the corridor. Rock quality is poor throughout, improving slightly toward the left above the third bolt, which is also the hardest spot.

current.area_walk_in: The formation stands to the left (west) of the trail just after the fourth footbridge, and its left end is marked by the deep Flimsy Flume chimney.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Lower Right Ski Track
beta: Start on holes slanting leftward past one bolt, then pull up a corner that leans left and crosses an overhang to reach a ledge. From there continue up the second pitch or leave rightward.
overview: Holes that angle left lead past one bolt to a leaning corner capped by a roof, ending on a ledge; either keep going above or bail rightward.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Lucas Palucas
beta: Use the bucket holds trending rightward to the first bolt, then angle left past three further bolts to the top.
overview: Buckets trend rightward toward one bolt, after which the line curves left, clipping another three.

current.area_walk_in: The corridor slices into the southeast flank of the Screamer Rocks mass, directly across from the spot where the path toward Rubicon forks left. Six routes line its walls.
current.descent: rappel down the back side
current.location: wall on the right in the valley next to the Brit Corridor entrance

name: Lunch is for Wimps
beta: Begin at a bolt immediately right of the previous route, then trend rightward, keeping near the arete on the formation's right side.

current.location: begins at a bolt next to the neighbouring line; trends right along the formation's right arete

name: Machete Direct
beta: The first pitch is strenuous free climbing on the ladder of old aid bolts.
overview: A long line up Machete Ridge, popular as big-wall practice. Done as aid it uses a series of old bolt ladders; free, the first four pitches have overhanging, difficult cruxes.

current.area_walk_in: From the west side lot, walk the Balconies Trail for about 0.6 miles to the junction with the Balconies Cave Trail, then follow the climbers' path marked with carabiner signs up to the base.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Obscure Destiny
beta:
From a ledge slanting up and left beneath the highest trees, climb two corners up to a block, then pass a bolt plus the crux to reach a second bolt. Go up-left, then up-right until a fixed pin appears.

Traverse straight left, then work back up rightward, arriving at a horizontal crack. Hard mantle and face moves lead beyond a third bolt onto a two-pin stance. One easier pitch finishes it.
overview: A pair of corners facing right lead to a block. Three bolts follow, with the crux between the first two, plus a traverse and a mantle that reaches a level crack. A lighter final pitch finishes it.

current.descent: descend rightward over forested ledges, then one short rap
current.location: separating Marmot Dome from the western wall, left of the faint break; starts on a ledge slanting left near the highest trees

name: Melvin
beta: Pass the first bolt shared with Racing Stripes, then exit up and rightward onto the overhanging headwall beside the crack; the steep, dynamic moves up there are the payoff.
overview: Steep, dynamic climbing up the final headwall. It starts past the first bolt shared with Racing Stripes, then exits up and right onto an overhanging headwall.

current.area_walk_in: Roughly a quarter hour on marked trails from the Bear Gulch day-use area.

name: Mesopotamia
beta: Move up the face, clipping four bolts, and stay with the faint dark streak.
overview: A face line tracking a faint streak of water-staining, tucked behind a cluster of large boulders and protected by four bolts.

current.location: tucked behind a group of large boulders, following a pale drip stain

name: Midnight Lumber
beta: Begin beside a juniper and climb flakes facing left up to a ramp, then pass a bolt (which may no longer be there) en route to the finish.
overview: Left-facing flakes lead to a ramp, then a bolt (possibly gone) and the top.

current.location: begins beside a juniper

name: Mike's Books
beta: Start from ledges on the face's left side and climb rightward into a crack within an open book; two flakes beneath the corner give harder direct starts. Follow the corner up to a big bolted ledge, then step left into a second corner and finish via a short face with one bolt.
overview: Two corner pitches with a bolted ledge between them; it is also one of the usual ways back down the formation.

current.descent: two rappels down the route

name: Modern Warfare
beta: Start by the detached flake at the base, follow the straight-in crack, and expect to work over a bulge close to the top.
overview: A straight-in crack with a loose flake at the foot and a bulge to pass near the top.

name: More Crazy Than Lazy
beta: Begin beside a bush, working a slender left-facing flake up under a small roof, then continue beyond two bolts onto a belay ledge. Pitch two follows either the crack overhead or the face on its right, which has one bolt (perhaps two).
overview: A slender flake leads to a little roof, and two bolts carry on to a ledge. A second pitch offers a crack or the face beside it.

current.area_walk_in: This little wall faces the Whispering Wall from the south-southwest; pass through a gap leading away from that wall's foot, or loop around the canyon entrance.

overview: A dihedral protected by a bolt, then rightward by a further bolt and a ledge-like break to the finish.

beta: After clipping the fourth bolt, head rightward around the arete and finish upward.
